text:
Maria: FYI I saw a 12% GPU memory jump on master after the kernel picker change this morning. Not consistent but spikes on long-seq runs. :thinking_face:
Aj: ugh. which kernel switch? the attention tiling change?
Maria: yes, the "kernel-tile-v2" gating landed at 06:12. Repro steps: run long-seq perf test (seq=4096) with cb enabled + kv warmup. saw OOMs on 2/8 runs.
Chloe: can you paste the allocator trace? even a short snippet helps
Maria: sure, attaching quick copy from the allocator logs:
```
alloc 0x7f.. size=3.2G tag=batch_workspace seq=4096
alloc 0x8a.. size=1.1G tag=kv_cache shard=0
free 0x7f.. tag=batch_workspace
alloc 0x7f.. size=3.6G tag=batch_workspace pad=4%
OOM on alloc 0x90.. size=256M tag=attention_scratch
```
Aj: interesting, workspace grew after kernel switch (3.2G -> 3.6G). sounds like kernel switched to a path that needs extra scratch per head.
Ryan: do we have kernel selection logs per-request? perf-bot should have traces for that rollout.
perf-bot: rollout "kernel-tile-v2" at 2026-03-15T06:12 by simon; sampled 5% of requests on prod-gpu-pool-1; avg scratch delta ~+9.7% for seq>2048.
Simon: That aligns. I thought the new kernel reduces compute but uses a larger temporary matrix for tiled matmul when seq length crosses 1024. Missed the memory impact on cb batching because packing increases peak.
Aj: cb (continuous batching) means batch growth can amplify per-seq scratch. if we have many mid-length sequences that get extended, padding waste + scratch multiply.
Maria: proposal: add per-kernel scratch estimate into the kernel catalog and let allocator reserve additional headroom when kernel chosen may increase workspace. This would avoid last-minute kernel-induced OOMs.
Chloe: also want better telemetry: attribute GPU mem usage to categories: model_weights, kv_cache, batch_workspace, kernel_scratch. Right now we only have coarse buckets.
Ryan: we can repurpose pad-occupancy telemetry to show effective per-seq overhead vector across batch growth. quick prototype: record "seq_len_at_enqueue" and "seq_len_at_dispatch" and compute delta per-request.
Simon: also consider conservative reclaim on kv_cache: if batch_workspace needs extra, attempt async eviction of cold entries before failing an alloc. But careful with tail-latency and hot keys.
Maria: I tried a small experiment locally: on a run with cb enabled, I forced kernel to v1 and allocator kept peak ~3.18G. with v2 it spiked to 3.65G and caused 1 OOM in 20 runs.
Aj: can you run a quick A/B on dedicated-qa with 1000 samples? we need distribution not single-run.
Maria: starting now, will dump telemetry to /tmp/kernel-mem-audit-1775.json
perf-bot: spawned perf job job-8874 on dedicated-qa at 2026-03-15T12:05; expected duration ~45m.
infra-bot: note: dedicated-qa pool has older cudnn that may change kernel selection. config: cudnn=8.3, cuda=11.7.
Chloe: thanks infra-bot. for fairness, keep cudnn/cuda consistent across A/B, otherwise kernel selector may behave differently.
Ryan: long-term: kernel metadata should include memory-cost function f(seq,heads,dim) so runtime can predict scratch for a given batch occupancy distribution. then compute a conservative padding budget = max(kernel_scratch) * safety_factor + dynamic_padding_waste_estimate.
Aj: agree. also add a graceful fallback: if predicted headroom insufficient, force kernel fallback to lower-memory path or schedule the larger batch onto a less-loaded device.
Simon: and add a small async reclaim window where kv_cache evicts LRU entries with cold-score < threshold before granting the workspace. We already track access timestamps so scoring is cheap.
Maria: ok action items:
- Aj: run A/B and post result (dedicated-qa) (ETA 1h)
- Ryan: prototype kernel memory-cost function and add to catalog schema (ETA 2d)
- Chloe: expand telemetry to the 4 memory buckets and record seq_len_at_enqueue/dispatch (ETA 2d)
- Simon: prototype async kv reclaim with safety cutoff and metric for false-evicts (ETA 3d)
- Maria: collect and attach allocator traces and sample logs from perf job (ETA 45m)
Aj: ack. I'll upload results as a short thread when done. :thumbsup:
Maria: thanks – if we can stop these sporadic OOMs before the next deploy it's huge.
Simon: one more note: we should add a regression alert that triggers when kernel rollout correlates with >5% increase in peak-workspace across sampled runs. automated email to eng-runtime.
Chloe: ok I'll wire that into the perf signal after we get the new telemetry.
Maria: closing for now, will post the perf dump when finished. :eyes:
